I have been farming this land for 55 years, so I know what works here in Quzhou. My main income comes from chili — that is my system. But I keep about 4 mu in the old winter wheat–summer maize rotation because grain is steady money and feeds the household. The other 6 mu I put in chili. At 72, my back is not what it was, so I hire help during chili transplanting and harvest. My son helps when he can.

For chili, I plant the improved hybrid line — I think it is "Xianjiao 8" type, what the dealer in town carries. Hybrid seed costs more but the yield and disease tolerance pay back. Chili is a heavy feeder. I put down about 4 cubic meters of chicken manure per mu before transplanting, then use compound fertilizer (15-15-15) at planting and topdress with urea twice during fruiting. In total that gives me roughly 28 kg N, 14 kg P, 22 kg K per mu. Chili really wants potassium for fruit set and color. I irrigate from my well — about 10 times across the season because chili cannot stand drought during flowering. Pests are my worst headache: aphids, thrips, anthracnose. I spray maybe 8 times. I rotary till before transplanting since the soil here is loamy and the seedlings need a fine bed.

For winter wheat, I plant the improved Jimai variety. Standard rates: 14 kg N, 7 kg P, 5 kg K per mu, with most N as topdressing at jointing. Two irrigations — winter and jointing. Plough every few years; rotary in between. Pesticide twice for aphids and powdery mildew.

For summer maize after wheat, hybrid seed (Zhengdan 958 or similar). 16 kg N, 6 kg P, 6 kg K. No-till direct seed into wheat stubble — saves labor and moisture. One irrigation if rains are short. Two pesticide passes for borer and armyworm.

I would rather spend a few extra yuan on fertilizer than watch my chili stunt. A failed chili crop loses me the year.
